editorial:
Imagine the pressure of having a massive hit for your first book and then having everyone expect your second one to be even better. That is exactly where you find Joe. He is a young guy who just wants to tell his story, but he is surrounded by friends and family who won't stop giving him their two cents. The movie starts off feeling like a normal drama about success, but it quickly turns into something much heavier. You can really feel Joe's stress as he stops listening to his own heart and starts obsessing over what everyone else thinks of him. It is a slow burn that makes you feel like you are right there in the room with him as he loses his grip.

The acting is the best part here because you can see the change in Joe's face as he gets more stressed. The pacing starts a bit slow, but the tension builds up until the ending hits you hard. If you like stories about how fame can mess with your head, you will love this. For the best experience, you should definitely stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the small details in the scenes. If you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great move for the high quality.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Joe completely breaks down because he tried too hard to please everyone. He realizes that the voices of his critics have replaced his own thoughts. The big twist is that Joe never actually finished the book; he spent all his time worrying about the reviews instead of writing. He ends up alone and empty, showing that chasing perfection based on other people's opinions only leads to failure.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character studies and stories about the dark side of success.
